title: Filesystem Search
subtitle: find, locate, and grep — flip to reveal meaning

cards.meaning: find = files matching criteria on the live tree; locate = fast name search via DB (can be stale); grep = lines inside files
cards.notes: find walks the tree; locate is a phone book of names; grep searches inside files

cards.meaning: Look for files and directories that match criteria on the live directory tree
cards.notes: You almost always care about path (where to start) and expression (match/do). Start narrow — find / walks the whole machine

cards.meaning: Match the basename (not the whole path)
Quote globs so the shell does not expand them before find sees them
For each match, run rm with that path substituted for {}; \; ends the -exec
Print paths, then xargs batches them as arguments to rm (fewer process starts)
cards.notes: Presented as equal to -exec rm {} \; for deleting core files under /tmp

cards.meaning: Null-separated paths — safe if names have spaces
-mtime, -size, -perm, -maxdepth, and more — learn with man find
Find files/directories by name using its database — not a live walk; fast but can be stale
cards.notes: Fast because it does not crawl the disk

cards.meaning: Rebuild the locate database (usually as root) so locate sees current names
cards.notes: New file missing? updatedb then locate, or use find

cards.meaning: Print lines that match a pattern (can be a regular expression)
cards.notes: find/locate = which files; grep = which lines
